document.title: TFX01: SITREP 5: Pakistan/Afghanistan Reaction to U.S. Air Strikes
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), 1998 Missile Strikes on Bin Laden May Have Backfired
document.note: [Confidential] Pakistan remains largely calm after the August 20 strikes. A Pakistani newspaper claims Mullah Omar is displeased with bin Laden for threatening retaliation and for undermining his control of Afghanistan's international relations. Excised.

events.description: US strikes on Usama bin Ladin's terrorist network, including Khost
Mob invaded US Embassy Kabul premises, pushing through Taliban guards
Zawahiri passed threat to avenge US strikes on behalf of bin Ladin
Taliban inner shura meeting over 22-23 Aug weekend where concerns about bin Ladin were reportedly expressed
Yusufzai phoned Mullah Omar, who said there cannot be two parallel emirates
The News published report of Omar's displeasure and planned emissary to bin Ladin
US strikes on bin Laden's terrorist network, targeting camps near Khost.
Mob invaded the US Embassy Kabul premises, pushing past Taliban guards and causing property damage.
Zawahiri passed a threat of revenge for the US strikes on behalf of bin Ladin.
Mullah Omar spoke by phone to Rahimullah Yusufzai, expressing displeasure at bin Ladin and rejecting parallel emirates.
The News published Yusufzai's report on Omar's displeasure with bin Ladin.
Embassy POLCOUNS discussed Pakistani reaction with Nishat Ahmed (reported as Monday meeting).
Pakistani authorities warned expatriates to leave northern Pakistan and barred foreigners from tribal territories; Islamabad CG spoke with Gilgit DC.
Press reported an unexploded cruise missile found in the Kharan desert, Balochistan.
Zawahiri passes a threat on behalf of bin Ladin to avenge the U.S. strikes.
Yusufzai speaks by phone with Mullah Omar, who says there cannot be two parallel emirates in Afghanistan.
The News article reports Omar displeased with bin Ladin and sending an emissary urging restraint.
Taliban spokesman Mullah Abdullah says bin Ladin's movements are restricted and he is protected by Taliban forces.
Afghan contacts, including a former resistance commander and tribal leader, meet U.S. Embassy political officer and say Omar is under pressure over bin Ladin.
Taliban Inner Shura meeting reportedly held over the weekend of August 22-23, where concerns about bin Ladin were purportedly expressed.

key_claims: Mullah Omar reportedly was displeased with bin Ladin's threats and said there cannot be two parallel emirates in Afghanistan.
Omar was reportedly sending an emissary to urge bin Ladin to show restraint.
Afghan contacts said Omar was under growing pressure from other Taliban leaders over bin Ladin's presence, with Mullah Hassan taking the lead.
A Taliban spokesman said bin Ladin's movements were restricted and that Taliban forces protect him.
The Taliban spread inaccurate reports of a strike near Jalalabad in Nangarhar.
Pakistan stayed largely calm, while the Kabul US embassy was invaded by a mob reportedly instigated by the Taliban.
